correctness.rationale: Complete exact proof: use orthogonal coordinates and sphere chord endpoints to derive the if-and-only-if shadow criterion. Concavity of each horizontal superlevel set identifies the unique bounded missing component as an intersection of two ellipses, then one-variable integration gives its area and strict monotonicity. Taylor expansion gives the 3/2 and 2/3 exponents and explicit coefficients. Uniform absolute axial cosine gives the random law; algebraic recovery from classical volume is unique. The standalone independent quadrature, ray test, critical asymptotic, and isotropic indicator program passed 6,824 numerical diagnostics; the proof does not depend on them. Boundaries theta=0 and theta=theta_c are treated explicitly.
